- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 3–7 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–15% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day moving average if sentiment is erratic.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment is negative or price is falling.
- If sentiment is near zero (0.0–0.1) and price is declining, model tends to underestimate; forecast should be 2–5% higher than true outcome to account for sentiment drag.
